sentence: Which phrase emphasizes preventing the crisis from occurring, rather than limiting one already underway?
setupText: A replacement generator was connected before the aquarium's life-support systems stopped working.
taskText: Which phrase emphasizes preventing the crisis from occurring, rather than limiting one already underway?
text: A replacement generator was connected before the aquarium's life-support systems stopped working. Which phrase emphasizes preventing the crisis from occurring, rather than limiting one already underway?
focusKey: coverage-collocations-c2-701:Avert versus contain or weather a crisis
explanation: Avert a crisis means prevent a threatened crisis from happening.

rationales.contain a crisis: Contain limits the spread or severity of a crisis that exists.
rationales.resolve a crisis: Resolve brings an existing crisis to an end rather than specifically prevents it.
rationales.avert a crisis: Avert a crisis means prevent a threatened crisis from happening.
rationales.weather a crisis: Weather means endure a crisis successfully, not prevent its occurrence.

sentence: Which phrase marks useful results without implying the work is finished or financially profitable?
setupText: Years of patient work on the adult-literacy project have finally helped several participants read independently, although classes are continuing.
taskText: Which phrase marks useful results without implying the work is finished or financially profitable?
text: Years of patient work on the adult-literacy project have finally helped several participants read independently, although classes are continuing. Which phrase marks useful results without implying the work is finished or financially profitable?
focusKey: coverage-collocations-c2-702:Bear fruit versus break even or gather pace
explanation: Bear fruit means produce worthwhile results; it does not require completion or profit.

rationales.bear fruit: Bear fruit means produce worthwhile results; it does not require completion or profit.
rationales.break even: Break even concerns income matching costs, not simply useful discoveries.
rationales.run its course: Run its course suggests a process proceeding to its natural end, unlike the continuing search.
rationales.gather pace: Gather pace means accelerate, which does not itself establish useful results.

sentence: Which phrase describes this practical power without assigning formal authority?
setupText: The retired designer has no official role, yet her opinions strongly shape which projects the association supports.
taskText: Which phrase describes this practical power without assigning formal authority?
text: The retired designer has no official role, yet her opinions strongly shape which projects the association supports. Which phrase describes this practical power without assigning formal authority?
focusKey: coverage-collocations-c2-703:Wield influence versus hold formal office
explanation: Wield influence means use or possess an effective ability to shape outcomes, without necessarily holding office.

rationales.hold executive office: Holding office would give a formal role, which the sentence excludes.
rationales.exercise statutory powers: Statutory powers arise from legal authority, not the informal influence described.
rationales.enjoy ceremonial status: Ceremonial status need not affect decisions; her opinions have a practical effect.
rationales.wield considerable influence: Wield influence means use or possess an effective ability to shape outcomes, without necessarily holding office.

sentence: Which phrase says the design survived critical examination, not merely received it?
setupText: Independent reviewers challenged the proposed bridge design in detail, but its safety calculations remained convincing after their examination.
taskText: Which phrase says the design survived critical examination, not merely received it?
text: Independent reviewers challenged the proposed bridge design in detail, but its safety calculations remained convincing after their examination. Which phrase says the design survived critical examination, not merely received it?
focusKey: coverage-collocations-c2-704:Withstand versus undergo scrutiny
explanation: Withstand scrutiny means remain defensible or convincing under close examination.

rationales.underwent scrutiny: Undergoing scrutiny means being examined; it does not specify whether the design survived the challenge.
rationales.withstood scrutiny: Withstand scrutiny means remain defensible or convincing under close examination.
rationales.escaped scrutiny: Escaping scrutiny means avoiding examination, contrary to the reviewers' work.
rationales.invited scrutiny: Inviting scrutiny prompts examination rather than describes surviving it.

sentence: Which phrase best describes functional ability without claiming deep mastery?
setupText: The conservator can use Italian manuals for routine repairs, but relies on a translator for complex historical arguments.
taskText: Which phrase best describes functional ability without claiming deep mastery?
text: The conservator can use Italian manuals for routine repairs, but relies on a translator for complex historical arguments. Which phrase best describes functional ability without claiming deep mastery?
focusKey: coverage-collocations-c2-705:Working knowledge versus slight familiarity or mastery
explanation: Working knowledge is enough to use something for practical purposes, without implying comprehensive mastery.

rationales.an intimate knowledge of Italian: Intimate knowledge suggests depth and familiarity beyond the practical ability described.
rationales.a nodding acquaintance with Italian: A nodding acquaintance suggests only slight familiarity, less than routinely using manuals.
rationales.a working knowledge of Italian: Working knowledge is enough to use something for practical purposes, without implying comprehensive mastery.
rationales.a passing interest in Italian: Interest describes curiosity, not the ability to work with the language.

sentence: Which phrase names presenting material as support, rather than interpreting it or drawing a conclusion from it?
setupText: In a formal essay, the author cites dated letters in support of her account of the journey.
taskText: Which phrase names presenting material as support, rather than interpreting it or drawing a conclusion from it?
text: In a formal essay, the author cites dated letters in support of her account of the journey. Which phrase names presenting material as support, rather than interpreting it or drawing a conclusion from it?
focusKey: coverage-collocations-c2-706:Adduce evidence versus interpret it or infer from it
explanation: Adduce evidence means bring evidence forward in support of an argument or claim.

rationales.adduce evidence: Adduce evidence means bring evidence forward in support of an argument or claim.
rationales.interpret evidence: Interpreting establishes what the material means rather than names its presentation as support.
rationales.infer a conclusion: Inferring draws a conclusion from material rather than supplies the supporting material.
rationales.qualify a conclusion: Qualifying limits or modifies a conclusion, not presents evidence for it.

sentence: Which phrase expresses invalidating the argument, not merely limiting or restating its conclusion?
setupText: The argument assumes the very conclusion it claims to prove. The editor regards that circularity as fatal to the reasoning.
taskText: Which phrase expresses invalidating the argument, not merely limiting or restating its conclusion?
text: The argument assumes the very conclusion it claims to prove. The editor regards that circularity as fatal to the reasoning. Which phrase expresses invalidating the argument, not merely limiting or restating its conclusion?
focusKey: coverage-collocations-c2-707:Vitiate an argument versus qualify a conclusion
explanation: Vitiate an argument means impair its validity or effectiveness; here the circularity is presented as fatal.

rationales.qualify the conclusion: Qualifying narrows a conclusion; the identified defect undermines the argument's validity.
rationales.amplify the claim: Amplifying expands or emphasizes a claim rather than invalidates the reasoning.
rationales.corroborate the reasoning: Corroborating supports the reasoning, opposite to identifying a fatal defect.
rationales.vitiate the argument: Vitiate an argument means impair its validity or effectiveness; here the circularity is presented as fatal.

sentence: Choose the phrase meaning 'limit that freedom without abolishing it'.
setupText: The guidelines leave curators room for judgment but set boundaries around which loans they may approve.
taskText: Choose the phrase meaning 'limit that freedom without abolishing it'.
text: The guidelines leave curators room for judgment but set boundaries around which loans they may approve. Choose the phrase meaning 'limit that freedom without abolishing it'.
focusKey: coverage-collocations-c2-708:Circumscribe versus remove or exercise discretion
explanation: 'Circumscribe discretion' means place limits around the scope of judgment someone may exercise.

rationales.remove discretion: Removing discretion leaves no room for judgment, stronger than the stated boundaries.
rationales.circumscribe discretion: 'Circumscribe discretion' means place limits around the scope of judgment someone may exercise.
rationales.exercise discretion: Exercising discretion uses the freedom, rather than sets its boundaries.
rationales.expand discretion: Expanding increases freedom rather than limits it.

sentence: Which sentence reports the reviewer's interpretation without adding endorsement or a demonstrated intention?
setupText: A reviewer reads the novel's abrupt ending as a refusal to offer the reader comfort. The author's own explanation is unknown.
taskText: Which sentence reports the reviewer's interpretation without adding endorsement or a demonstrated intention?
text: A reviewer reads the novel's abrupt ending as a refusal to offer the reader comfort. The author's own explanation is unknown. Which sentence reports the reviewer's interpretation without adding endorsement or a demonstrated intention?
options: The reviewer established the author's refusal to offer comfort.
The reviewer construed the ending as a refusal to offer comfort.
The reviewer elicited the author's refusal to offer comfort.
The reviewer endorsed the ending as a refusal to offer comfort.
answer: The reviewer construed the ending as a refusal to offer comfort.
focusKey: coverage-collocations-c2-709:Construe something as versus establish an intention
explanation: Construe something as means interpret it in a particular way; it attributes a reading without proving intention.

rationales.The reviewer established the author's re: Established presents the intention as demonstrated rather than as the reviewer's reading.
rationales.The reviewer elicited the author's refus: Elicited implies obtaining that response from the author, whose explanation is unknown.
rationales.The reviewer construed the ending as a r: Construe something as means interpret it in a particular way; it attributes a reading without proving intention.
rationales.The reviewer endorsed the ending as a re: Endorsed adds approval of the ending; identifying a meaning does not itself express approval.

sentence: Choose the phrase for supporting the allegation with evidence, not merely making it public.
setupText: The match official said the original score sheets supported her allegation that tournament results had been altered.
taskText: Choose the phrase for supporting the allegation with evidence, not merely making it public.
text: The match official said the original score sheets supported her allegation that tournament results had been altered. Choose the phrase for supporting the allegation with evidence, not merely making it public.
focusKey: coverage-collocations-c2-710:Substantiate versus publicize or reiterate an allegation
explanation: Substantiate an allegation means provide supporting evidence for it.

rationales.substantiate the allegation: Substantiate an allegation means provide supporting evidence for it.
rationales.publicize the allegation: Publicizing makes it widely known, whether or not support is supplied.
rationales.reiterate the allegation: Reiterating repeats it rather than adds evidential support.
rationales.withdraw the allegation: Withdrawing takes it back rather than supports it.

sentence: Which phrase best captures the overall reception?
setupText: Applause at the premiere was brief. Reviews called the performance 'competent' and 'pleasant enough', but expressed little interest in seeing it again.
taskText: Which phrase best captures the overall reception?
text: Applause at the premiere was brief. Reviews called the performance 'competent' and 'pleasant enough', but expressed little interest in seeing it again. Which phrase best captures the overall reception?
focusKey: coverage-collocations-c2-711:Lukewarm versus frosty or polarized reception
explanation: Lukewarm reception describes an unenthusiastic or only mildly favorable response without necessarily implying hostility.

rationales.a frosty reception: Frosty suggests coldness or hostility, stronger than polite lack of enthusiasm.
rationales.a rapturous reception: Rapturous describes intense delight, opposite to the limited enthusiasm.
rationales.a polarized reception: The described responses show limited enthusiasm, not sharply opposed camps.
rationales.a lukewarm reception: Lukewarm reception describes an unenthusiastic or only mildly favorable response without necessarily implying hostility.

sentence: Which phrase presents tradition as a reason or authority, not merely as a subject of study?
setupText: To justify keeping the ceremony unchanged, the chair appealed to the practice of earlier generations.
taskText: Which phrase presents tradition as a reason or authority, not merely as a subject of study?
text: To justify keeping the ceremony unchanged, the chair appealed to the practice of earlier generations. Which phrase presents tradition as a reason or authority, not merely as a subject of study?
focusKey: coverage-collocations-c2-712:Invoke tradition versus document or revive it
explanation: Invoke tradition means appeal to established practice as a reason or authority.

rationales.document tradition: Documenting records practices without necessarily using them to justify a decision.
rationales.invoke tradition: Invoke tradition means appeal to established practice as a reason or authority.
rationales.revive tradition: Reviving restores a discontinued practice; the issue here is keeping a current one.
rationales.reinterpret tradition: Reinterpreting gives tradition a new reading rather than necessarily appeals to it as authority.

sentence: Which phrase describes countering that presumption with contrary evidence?
setupText: The food historian presumed that the recipe originated locally. An older printed version from another country contradicted that account.
taskText: Which phrase describes countering that presumption with contrary evidence?
text: The food historian presumed that the recipe originated locally. An older printed version from another country contradicted that account. Which phrase describes countering that presumption with contrary evidence?
focusKey: coverage-collocations-c2-713:Rebut versus entertain or articulate a presumption
explanation: Rebut a presumption means counter it with argument or evidence to the contrary.

rationales.entertain the presumption: Entertaining considers it as a possibility, not counters it.
rationales.articulate the presumption: Articulating expresses it clearly without disproving it.
rationales.rebut the presumption: Rebut a presumption means counter it with argument or evidence to the contrary.
rationales.revive the presumption: Reviving restores an assumption previously set aside, opposite to the older recipe's role.

sentence: Which phrase expresses that assessment without suggesting the costs outweighed the achievement?
setupText: The exhibition achieved its main aim of attracting new visitors, although its audio guides needed improvement. The organizer wants an overall positive assessment with that reservation.
taskText: Which phrase expresses that assessment without suggesting the costs outweighed the achievement?
text: The exhibition achieved its main aim of attracting new visitors, although its audio guides needed improvement. The organizer wants an overall positive assessment with that reservation. Which phrase expresses that assessment without suggesting the costs outweighed the achievement?
focusKey: coverage-collocations-c2-714:Qualified success versus Pyrrhic victory
explanation: A qualified success is a success with reservations or limitations, not an unreserved triumph.

rationales.a qualified success: A qualified success is a success with reservations or limitations, not an unreserved triumph.
rationales.an unqualified success: Unqualified removes the reservations that the organizer wants to retain.
rationales.a Pyrrhic victory: A Pyrrhic victory comes at such a cost that the achievement is undermined; that is not the intended assessment.
rationales.an outright failure: Outright failure contradicts the achievement of the main aim.

a practical grasp of the subject

focusKey: coverage-collocations-c2-715:Tenuous grasp versus firm or practical grasp
explanation: Tenuous grasp describes understanding that is weak, uncertain or easily lost.

rationales.a firm grasp of the subject: Firm grasp suggests secure understanding, contrary to the uncertainty in application.
rationales.a broad grasp of the subject: Broad describes range; it does not specifically characterize understanding as fragile.
rationales.a practical grasp of the subject: Practical grasp suggests the ability to use the knowledge, which is the trainee's weakness.
rationales.a tenuous grasp of the subject: Tenuous grasp describes understanding that is weak, uncertain or easily lost.

focusKey: coverage-collocations-c2-716:Searching questions versus leading or closed questions
explanation: Searching questions probe closely and critically into an issue or its underlying reasons.

rationales.leading questions: Leading questions steer people toward a suggested answer, not simply probe deeply.
rationales.searching questions: Searching questions probe closely and critically into an issue or its underlying reasons.
rationales.closed questions: Closed questions restrict the response format; they need not probe deeply.
rationales.rhetorical questions: Rhetorical questions make a point rather than primarily seek the participant's answer.

sentence: Which phrase identifies the example's role as a concrete instance, not the invention or derivation of the principle?
setupText: The article states a principle of anonymous judging. Its next section describes a competition in which names were removed before entries were assessed.

focusKey: coverage-collocations-c2-717:Instantiate versus formulate or derive a principle
explanation: Instantiate a principle means provide a concrete instance of it.

rationales.formulate the principle: Formulating devises or states the principle, which the article has already done.
rationales.derive the principle: Deriving reasons toward a principle; this example is presented after it as an instance.
rationales.instantiate the principle: Instantiate a principle means provide a concrete instance of it.
rationales.qualify the principle: Qualifying limits or modifies the principle rather than simply exemplifies it.

sentence: Which interpretation preserves the negative phrase without turning it into a prediction of success?
setupText: The report says that disagreements over style do not preclude cooperation on restoring the theater.
taskText: Which interpretation preserves the negative phrase without turning it into a prediction of success?
text: The report says that disagreements over style do not preclude cooperation on restoring the theater. Which interpretation preserves the negative phrase without turning it into a prediction of success?
options: The disagreements ensure the partners will cooperate.
The disagreements have already been resolved through cooperation.
The disagreements do not make cooperation impossible.
The disagreements postpone cooperation until agreement on style is reached.
answer: The disagreements do not make cooperation impossible.
focusKey: coverage-collocations-c2-718:Do not preclude cooperation without predicting it
explanation: Do not preclude means do not rule out; it leaves cooperation possible without promising it.

rationales.The disagreements do not make cooperatio: Do not preclude means do not rule out; it leaves cooperation possible without promising it.
rationales.The disagreements ensure the partners wi: Not ruling out cooperation is weaker than ensuring it will happen.
rationales.The disagreements have already been reso: The phrase states neither resolution nor an event already completed.
rationales.The disagreements postpone cooperation u: The phrase does not make stylistic agreement a prerequisite for cooperation.

sentence: Which phrase uses 'distinction' to mean 'honor', not 'a difference between categories'?
setupText: The prestigious award brought honor to an ensemble that had previously been little known.
taskText: Which phrase uses 'distinction' to mean 'honor', not 'a difference between categories'?
text: The prestigious award brought honor to an ensemble that had previously been little known. Which phrase uses 'distinction' to mean 'honor', not 'a difference between categories'?
focusKey: coverage-collocations-c2-719:Confer distinction on versus draw a distinction between
explanation: 'Confer distinction on' means bestow honor or prestige; this partnership uses a different sense from 'draw a distinction'.

rationales.drew a distinction between ensembles: 'Draw a distinction' identifies a difference, not an honor bestowed.
rationales.maintained a distinction between ensembl: Maintaining a distinction preserves a difference between categories or groups.
rationales.blurred the distinction between ensemble: Blurring a distinction makes a difference less clear rather than confers honor.
rationales.conferred distinction on the ensemble: 'Confer distinction on' means bestow honor or prestige; this partnership uses a different sense from 'draw a distinction'.

sentence: Choose the phrase for fulfilling that duty, not being excused from it or passing it to someone else.
setupText: The festival volunteer promised to clear the shared kitchen and completed the work as agreed.
taskText: Choose the phrase for fulfilling that duty, not being excused from it or passing it to someone else.
text: The festival volunteer promised to clear the shared kitchen and completed the work as agreed. Choose the phrase for fulfilling that duty, not being excused from it or passing it to someone else.
focusKey: coverage-collocations-c2-720:Discharge versus waive, transfer or incur an obligation
explanation: Discharge an obligation means fulfill the duty or requirement.

rationales.waive the obligation: Waiving releases a requirement; the volunteer actually performed the promised work.
rationales.discharge the obligation: Discharge an obligation means fulfill the duty or requirement.
rationales.transfer the obligation: Transferring passes the duty to someone else rather than performs it.
rationales.incur the obligation: Incurring becomes subject to the duty, an earlier stage than fulfillment.
